passages.text: Now as Jesus was passing by, He saw a man blind from birth, and His disciples asked Him, “Rabbi, who sinned, this man or his parents, that he was born blind?”
passages.sermon:
Jesus was passing by.
He saw a man.
This man was blind from birth.
The disciples of Jesus spoke to Him.
They called Him Rabbi.
They asked Jesus a question.
They said, “Who sinned?”
They asked if this man sinned.
They also asked if his parents sinned.
They wanted to know why the man was born blind.
passages.original: Καὶ παράγων εἶδεν ἄνθρωπον τυφλὸν ἐκ γενετῆς καὶ ἠρώτησαν αὐτὸν οἱ μαθηταὶ αὐτοῦ λέγοντες Ῥαββί τίς ἥμαρτεν οὗτος ἢ οἱ γονεῖς αὐτοῦ ἵνα τυφλὸς γεννηθῇ

passages.text: Jesus answered, “Neither this man nor his parents sinned, but this happened so that the works of God would be displayed in him.
passages.sermon:
Jesus saw a man who was blind from birth.
His disciples asked Jesus about the cause of the man’s blindness.
They asked if the man sinned or if his parents sinned.
Jesus answered them.
Jesus said, “This man did not sin.
His parents did not sin.
He was born blind so that God’s works could be shown in him.”
passages.original: Ἀπεκρίθη Ἰησοῦς Οὔτε οὗτος ἥμαρτεν οὔτε οἱ γονεῖς αὐτοῦ ἀλλ’ ἵνα φανερωθῇ τὰ ἔργα τοῦ Θεοῦ ἐν αὐτῷ

passages.text: While it is daytime, we must do the works of Him who sent Me. Night is coming, when no one can work.
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to His disciples.
Jesus said, “God sent Me.”
We must do the works of God.
We must work while it is day.
Daytime is the time to work.
Night will come.
No one can work at night.
passages.original: ἡμᾶς δεῖ ἐργάζεσθαι τὰ ἔργα τοῦ πέμψαντός με ἕως ἡμέρα ἐστίν ἔρχεται νὺξ ὅτε οὐδεὶς δύναται ἐργάζεσθαι

passages.text: While I am in the world, I am the light of the world.”
passages.sermon: Jesus spoke to the people.\r\nJesus was present in the world.\r\nJesus said, “I am the light of the world.”
passages.original: ὅταν ἐν τῷ κόσμῳ ὦ φῶς εἰμι τοῦ κόσμου

passages.text: When Jesus had said this, He spit on the ground, made some mud, and applied it to the man’s eyes.
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke these words.
Jesus spit on the ground.
Jesus made mud from His spit.
Jesus took the mud.
Jesus put the mud on the man’s eyes.
passages.original: Ταῦτα εἰπὼν ἔπτυσεν χαμαὶ καὶ ἐποίησεν πηλὸν ἐκ τοῦ πτύσματος καὶ ἐπέχρισεν αὐτοῦ τὸν πηλὸν ἐπὶ τοὺς ὀφθαλμούς

passages.text: Then He told him, “Go, wash in the Pool of Siloam” (which means “Sent”). So the man went and washed, and came back seeing.
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to the man who was blind.
Jesus told him, “Go. Wash in the Pool of Siloam.”
The name Siloam means “Sent.”
The man went to the pool.
He washed in the pool.
He returned able to see.
passages.original: καὶ εἶπεν αὐτῷ Ὕπαγε νίψαι εἰς τὴν κολυμβήθραν τοῦ Σιλωάμ ὃ ἑρμηνεύεται Ἀπεσταλμένος ἀπῆλθεν οὖν καὶ ἐνίψατο καὶ ἦλθεν βλέπων

passages.text: At this, his neighbors and those who had formerly seen him begging began to ask, “Isn’t this the man who used to sit and beg?”
passages.sermon:
The man had been blind before.
He used to sit and beg.
His neighbors saw him.
Other people had seen him begging before.
These people began to ask a question.
They said, “Isn’t this the man who used to sit and beg?”
passages.original: Οἱ οὖν γείτονες καὶ οἱ θεωροῦντες αὐτὸν τὸ πρότερον ὅτι προσαίτης ἦν ἔλεγον Οὐχ οὗτός ἐστιν ὁ καθήμενος καὶ προσαιτῶν

passages.text: Some claimed that he was, but others said, “No, he just looks like him.” But the man kept saying, “I am the one.”
passages.sermon:
Some people said, "This is the man."
\r\nOther people said, "No, he only looks like the man."
\r\nThe man said, "I am the man."
passages.original: Ἄλλοι ἔλεγον ὅτι Οὗτός ἐστιν ἄλλοι ἔλεγον Οὐχί ἀλλὰ ὅμοιος αὐτῷ ἐστιν Ἐκεῖνος ἔλεγεν ὅτι Ἐγώ εἰμι

passages.text: “How then were your eyes opened?” they asked.
passages.sermon:
The neighbors saw the man who used to beg.
They knew he was once blind.
They saw that now he could see.
They asked him a question.
They said, "How were your eyes opened?"
passages.original: Ἔλεγον οὖν αὐτῷ Πῶς οὖν ἠνεῴχθησάν σου οἱ ὀφθαλμοί

passages.text: He answered, “The man they call Jesus made some mud and anointed my eyes, and He told me to go to Siloam and wash. So I went and washed and received my sight.”
passages.sermon:
A man named Jesus acted.
Jesus made some mud.
Jesus put the mud on my eyes.
Jesus spoke to me.
Jesus told me, "Go to Siloam and wash."
I went to Siloam.
I washed there.
After I washed, I could see.
passages.original: Ἀπεκρίθη ἐκεῖνος Ὁ ἄνθρωπος ὁ λεγόμενος Ἰησοῦς πηλὸν ἐποίησεν καὶ ἐπέχρισέν μου τοὺς ὀφθαλμοὺς καὶ εἶπέν μοι ὅτι Ὕπαγε εἰς τὸν Σιλωὰμ καὶ νίψαι ἀπελθὼν οὖν καὶ νιψάμενος ἀνέβλεψα

passages.text: “Where is He?” they asked. “I do not know,” he answered.
passages.sermon: The people spoke to the man who had been blind.\r\nThey asked him, “Where is Jesus?”\r\nThe man replied, “I do not know.”
passages.original: Καὶ εἶπαν αὐτῷ Ποῦ ἐστιν ἐκεῖνος Λέγει Οὐκ οἶδα

passages.text: They brought to the Pharisees the man who had been blind.
passages.sermon: The people brought the man to the Pharisees.\r\nThis man had been blind before.
passages.original: Ἄγουσιν αὐτὸν πρὸς τοὺς Φαρισαίους τόν ποτε τυφλόν

passages.text: Now the day on which Jesus had made the mud and opened his eyes was a Sabbath.
passages.sermon:
Jesus healed a man who had been blind.
Jesus made mud and put it on the man’s eyes.
Jesus did this on a Sabbath day.
The Sabbath was a special day of rest for the Jews.
passages.original: ἦν δὲ σάββατον ἐν ᾗ ἡμέρᾳ τὸν πηλὸν ἐποίησεν ὁ Ἰησοῦς καὶ ἀνέῳξεν αὐτοῦ τοὺς ὀφθαλμούς

passages.text: So the Pharisees also asked him how he had received his sight. The man answered, “He put mud on my eyes, and I washed, and now I can see.”
passages.sermon:
The Pharisees questioned the man who had been blind.
They asked him how he received his sight.
The man answered them.
He said, "He put mud on my eyes."
"I washed."
"Now I can see."
passages.original: πάλιν οὖν ἠρώτων αὐτὸν καὶ οἱ Φαρισαῖοι πῶς ἀνέβλεψεν Ὁ δὲ εἶπεν αὐτοῖς Πηλὸν ἐπέθηκέν μου ἐπὶ τοὺς ὀφθαλμούς καὶ ἐνιψάμην καὶ βλέπω

passages.text: Because of this, some of the Pharisees said, “This man is not from God, for He does not keep the Sabbath.” But others said, “How can a sinful man perform such signs?” And there was division among them.
passages.sermon:
Some Pharisees spoke about Jesus.
They said, “This man is not from God.”
They said this because Jesus did not keep the Sabbath.
Other Pharisees disagreed.
They said, “How can a sinful man do such signs?”
The Pharisees argued with each other.
They were divided.
passages.original: Ἔλεγον οὖν ἐκ τῶν Φαρισαίων τινές Οὐκ ἔστιν οὗτος παρὰ Θεοῦ ὁ ἄνθρωπος ὅτι τὸ σάββατον οὐ τηρεῖ Ἄλλοι δὲ ἔλεγον Πῶς δύναται ἄνθρωπος ἁμαρτωλὸς τοιαῦτα σημεῖα ποιεῖν Καὶ σχίσμα ἦν ἐν αὐτοῖς

passages.text: So once again they asked the man who had been blind, “What do you say about Him, since it was your eyes He opened?” “He is a prophet,” the man replied.
passages.sermon:
The Pharisees spoke to the man who had been blind.
They asked him again about Jesus.
They said, “What do you say about Him?”
They reminded the man, “He opened your eyes.”
The man answered them.
He said, “He is a prophet.”
passages.original: λέγουσιν οὖν τῷ τυφλῷ πάλιν Τί σὺ λέγεις περὶ αὐτοῦ ὅτι ἠνέῳξέν σου τοὺς ὀφθαλμούς Ὁ δὲ εἶπεν ὅτι Προφήτης ἐστίν

passages.text: The Jews still did not believe that the man had been blind and had received his sight until they summoned his parents and asked, “Is this your son, the one you say was born blind? So how is it that he can now see?”
passages.sermon:
The Jews did not believe the man had been blind.
The Jews did not believe he had received his sight.
They did not believe these things about him.
They did not believe until they called his parents.
They called the parents of the man who had received his sight.
They asked the parents a question.
They said, “Is this your son?”
They said, “Is this the one you say was born blind?”
They said, “How is it that he can now see?”
passages.original: Οὐκ ἐπίστευσαν οὖν οἱ Ἰουδαῖοι περὶ αὐτοῦ ὅτι ἦν τυφλὸς καὶ ἀνέβλεψεν ἕως ὅτου ἐφώνησαν τοὺς γονεῖς αὐτοῦ τοῦ ἀναβλέψαντος καὶ ἠρώτησαν αὐτοὺς λέγοντες Οὗτός ἐστιν ὁ υἱὸς ὑμῶν ὃν ὑμεῖς λέγετε ὅτι τυφλὸς ἐγεννήθη πῶς οὖν βλέπει ἄρτι

passages.text: His parents answered, “We know he is our son, and we know he was born blind.
passages.sermon:
The parents of the man spoke.
They answered the question.
They said, “We know this is our son.
We know he was born blind.”
passages.original: Ἀπεκρίθησαν οὖν οἱ γονεῖς αὐτοῦ καὶ εἶπαν Οἴδαμεν ὅτι οὗτός ἐστιν ὁ υἱὸς ἡμῶν καὶ ὅτι τυφλὸς ἐγεννήθη

passages.text: But how he can now see or who opened his eyes, we do not know. Ask him. He is old enough to speak for himself.”
passages.sermon:
His parents did not know how he could now see.
They did not know who opened his eyes.
They told the Jews to ask their son.
Their son was old enough to answer for himself.
He would speak about himself.
passages.original: πῶς δὲ νῦν βλέπει οὐκ οἴδαμεν ἢ τίς ἤνοιξεν αὐτοῦ τοὺς ὀφθαλμοὺς ἡμεῖς οὐκ οἴδαμεν αὐτὸν ἐρωτήσατε ἡλικίαν ἔχει αὐτὸς περὶ ἑαυτοῦ λαλήσει

passages.text: His parents said this because they were afraid of the Jews. For the Jews had already determined that anyone who confessed Jesus as the Christ would be put out of the synagogue.
passages.sermon:
His parents spoke these words.
They were afraid of the Jews.
The Jews had already made a decision.
They decided to put anyone out of the synagogue who confessed Jesus as the Christ.
passages.original: Ταῦτα εἶπαν οἱ γονεῖς αὐτοῦ ὅτι ἐφοβοῦντο τοὺς Ἰουδαίους ἤδη γὰρ συνετέθειντο οἱ Ἰουδαῖοι ἵνα ἐάν τις αὐτὸν ὁμολογήσῃ Χριστόν ἀποσυνάγωγος γένηται

passages.text: That was why his parents said, “He is old enough. Ask him.”
passages.sermon:
His parents were afraid of the Jews.
The Jews had already decided to put out of the synagogue anyone who confessed Jesus as the Christ.
Because of this, his parents said, “He is old enough.
Ask him.”
passages.original: διὰ τοῦτο οἱ γονεῖς αὐτοῦ εἶπαν ὅτι Ἡλικίαν ἔχει αὐτὸν ἐπερωτήσατε

passages.text: So a second time they called for the man who had been blind and said, “Give glory to God! We know that this man is a sinner.”
passages.sermon:
The Jewish leaders called the man who had been blind.
They called him a second time.
They spoke to him.
They said, “Give glory to God.”
They said, “We know this man is a sinner.”
They meant Jesus when they said “this man.”
passages.original: Ἐφώνησαν οὖν τὸν ἄνθρωπον ἐκ δευτέρου ὃς ἦν τυφλὸς καὶ εἶπαν αὐτῷ Δὸς δόξαν τῷ Θεῷ ἡμεῖς οἴδαμεν ὅτι οὗτος ὁ ἄνθρωπος ἁμαρτωλός ἐστιν

passages.text: He answered, “Whether He is a sinner I do not know. There is one thing I do know: I was blind, but now I see!”
passages.sermon:
The man had been blind.
The man answered them.
He said, “I do not know if He is a sinner.
I know one thing.
I was blind before.
Now I see.”
passages.original: Ἀπεκρίθη οὖν ἐκεῖνος Εἰ ἁμαρτωλός ἐστιν οὐκ οἶδα ἓν οἶδα ὅτι τυφλὸς ὢν ἄρτι βλέπω

passages.text: “What did He do to you?” they asked. “How did He open your eyes?”
passages.sermon:
The Pharisees questioned the man who had been blind.
They asked him about Jesus.
They said, “What did He do to you?”
They also asked, “How did He open your eyes?”
passages.original: Εἶπον οὖν αὐτῷ Τί ἐποίησέν σοι πῶς ἤνοιξέν σου τοὺς ὀφθαλμούς

passages.text: He replied, “I already told you, and you did not listen. Why do you want to hear it again? Do you also want to become His disciples?”
passages.sermon:
The man who was healed spoke to them.
He said, "I already told you."
"You did not listen."
"Why do you want to hear it again?"
"Do you also want to become His disciples?"
passages.original: Ἀπεκρίθη αὐτοῖς Εἶπον ὑμῖν ἤδη καὶ οὐκ ἠκούσατε τί πάλιν θέλετε ἀκούειν μὴ καὶ ὑμεῖς θέλετε αὐτοῦ μαθηταὶ γενέσθαι

passages.text: Then they heaped insults on him and said, “You are His disciple; we are disciples of Moses.
passages.sermon:
The Pharisees spoke to the man who had been blind.
They insulted him.
They said, "You are a disciple of that man."
They said, "We are disciples of Moses."
passages.original: Καὶ ἐλοιδόρησαν αὐτὸν καὶ εἶπον Σὺ μαθητὴς εἶ ἐκείνου ἡμεῖς δὲ τοῦ Μωϋσέως ἐσμὲν μαθηταί

passages.text: We know that God spoke to Moses, but we do not know where this man is from.”
passages.sermon: The Jewish leaders spoke to the man who had been healed.\r\nThey said, “We know that God spoke to Moses.\r\nWe do not know where this man is from.”
passages.original: ἡμεῖς οἴδαμεν ὅτι Μωϋσεῖ λελάληκεν ὁ Θεός τοῦτον δὲ οὐκ οἴδαμεν πόθεν ἐστίν

passages.text: “That is remarkable indeed!” the man said. “You do not know where He is from, and yet He opened my eyes.
passages.sermon:
A man spoke to the Pharisees.
He had been born blind.
Jesus healed him and gave him sight.
The man answered the Pharisees.
He said, “This is amazing.
You do not know where Jesus comes from.
But He opened my eyes.”
passages.original: Ἀπεκρίθη ὁ ἄνθρωπος καὶ εἶπεν αὐτοῖς Ἐν τούτῳ γὰρ τὸ θαυμαστόν ἐστιν ὅτι ὑμεῖς οὐκ οἴδατε πόθεν ἐστίν καὶ ἤνοιξέν μου τοὺς ὀφθαλμούς

passages.text: We know that God does not listen to sinners, but He does listen to the one who worships Him and does His will.
passages.sermon:
God does not listen to sinners.
God listens to people who worship Him.
God listens to people who do His will.
We know this is true.
passages.original: οἴδαμεν ὅτι ὁ Θεὸς ἁμαρτωλῶν οὐκ ἀκούει ἀλλ’ ἐάν τις θεοσεβὴς ᾖ καὶ τὸ θέλημα αὐτοῦ ποιῇ τούτου ἀκούει

passages.text: Never before has anyone heard of opening the eyes of a man born blind.
passages.sermon: A man was born blind.\r\nNo one ever heard of anyone opening the eyes of such a man.\r\nThis has never happened before in all history.
passages.original: ἐκ τοῦ αἰῶνος οὐκ ἠκούσθη ὅτι ἠνέῳξέν τις ὀφθαλμοὺς τυφλοῦ γεγεννημένου

passages.text: If this man were not from God, He could do no such thing.”
passages.sermon:
This man comes from God.
If this man were not from God, he could do nothing.
He could not perform any miracles without God.
God gives him power to do these things.
passages.original: εἰ μὴ ἦν οὗτος παρὰ Θεοῦ οὐκ ἠδύνατο ποιεῖν οὐδέν

passages.text: They replied, “You were born in utter sin, and you are instructing us?” And they threw him out.
passages.sermon:
The Pharisees spoke to the man who was born blind.
They said, “You were born completely in sin.”
They asked, “Do you teach us?”
They threw the man out.
passages.original: Ἀπεκρίθησαν καὶ εἶπαν αὐτῷ Ἐν ἁμαρτίαις σὺ ἐγεννήθης ὅλος καὶ σὺ διδάσκεις ἡμᾶς καὶ ἐξέβαλον αὐτὸν ἔξω

passages.text: When Jesus heard that they had thrown him out, He found the man and said, “Do you believe in the Son of Man ?”
passages.sermon:
Jesus is the Son of Man.
Jesus heard that they had thrown the man out.
Jesus found the man.
Jesus spoke to the man.
Jesus said, “Do you believe in the Son of Man?”
passages.original: Ἤκουσεν Ἰησοῦς ὅτι ἐξέβαλον αὐτὸν ἔξω καὶ εὑρὼν αὐτὸν εἶπεν Σὺ πιστεύεις εἰς τὸν Υἱὸν τοῦ ἀνθρώπου

passages.text: “Who is He, Sir?” he replied. “Tell me so that I may believe in Him.”
passages.sermon:
A man spoke to Jesus.
The man did not know who the Son of Man was.
He said, “Who is He, Sir?”
He wanted to believe in the Son of Man.
He said, “Tell me so that I may believe in Him.”
passages.original: Ἀπεκρίθη ἐκεῖνος καὶ εἶπεν Καὶ τίς ἐστιν Κύριε ἵνα πιστεύσω εἰς αὐτόν

passages.text: “You have already seen Him,” Jesus answered. “He is the One speaking with you.”
passages.sermon: Jesus spoke to the man.\r\nJesus said, “You have already seen Him.”\r\nJesus said, “The One speaking with you is He.”
passages.original: Εἶπεν αὐτῷ ὁ Ἰησοῦς Καὶ ἑώρακας αὐτὸν καὶ ὁ λαλῶν μετὰ σοῦ ἐκεῖνός ἐστιν

passages.text: “Lord, I believe,” he said. And he worshiped Jesus.
passages.sermon: The man spoke to Jesus.\r\nHe said, “Lord, I believe.”\r\nHe worshiped Jesus.
passages.original: Ὁ δὲ ἔφη Πιστεύω Κύριε καὶ προσεκύνησεν αὐτῷ

passages.text: Then Jesus declared, “For judgment I have come into this world, so that the blind may see and those who see may become blind.”
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to the people.
Jesus said he came into this world for judgment.
He said he came so that blind people may see.
He said he came so that people who see may become blind.
passages.original: Καὶ εἶπεν ὁ Ἰησοῦς Εἰς κρίμα ἐγὼ εἰς τὸν κόσμον τοῦτον ἦλθον ἵνα οἱ μὴ βλέποντες βλέπωσιν καὶ οἱ βλέποντες τυφλοὶ γένωνται

passages.text: Some of the Pharisees who were with Him heard this, and they asked Him, “Are we blind too?”
passages.sermon:
Some Pharisees stood with Jesus.
These Pharisees heard what Jesus said.
They spoke to Jesus.
They asked Jesus a question.
They said, “Are we blind too?”
passages.original: ἤκουσαν ἐκ τῶν Φαρισαίων ταῦτα οἱ μετ’ αὐτοῦ ὄντες καὶ εἶπον αὐτῷ Μὴ καὶ ἡμεῖς τυφλοί ἐσμεν

passages.text: “If you were blind,” Jesus replied, “you would not be guilty of sin. But since you claim you can see, your guilt remains.”
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to the Pharisees.
The Pharisees claimed they could see.
Jesus said, “If you were blind, you would not be guilty of sin.
But you say, ‘We see.’
So your guilt remains.”
passages.original: Εἶπεν αὐτοῖς ὁ Ἰησοῦς Εἰ τυφλοὶ ἦτε οὐκ ἂν εἴχετε ἁμαρτίαν νῦν δὲ λέγετε ὅτι Βλέπομεν ἡ ἁμαρτία ὑμῶν μένει
